Complementary information — The documents provide obesity data for different years, definitions (overweight vs. obese), and geographic scopes, which together inform the query without contradiction.

The evidence clusters by time period and measurement. d1 (2023) and d6 (2017/18) give recent provincial data for Canada, with d1 focusing on "overweight" and d6 on "obesity." d2 provides older (2004) provincial obesity rates. d3, d4, and d5 discuss U.S. states and global rankings, which are irrelevant to the query about a Canadian province. d7 discusses urban-rural disparities within Canada but does not rank provinces.

The query asks for the "most obese province," implying a Canadian context. d6 directly states Newfoundland and Labrador had the highest obesity prevalence (39.4%) in 2017/18 [d6]. d1, while about "overweight," identifies Alberta as having the highest share of overweight adults in 2023 [d1]. These are complementary because they refer to different metrics (obesity vs. overweight) and slightly different time periods. d2's older data shows Newfoundland and Labrador with a 34% obesity rate in 2004 [d2], consistent with the trend of it being high. The U.S.-focused documents (d3, d5) and global ranking (d4) are irrelevant. d7 provides context but no definitive ranking. Therefore, the most recent direct evidence on obesity prevalence points to Newfoundland and Labrador.

Based on the retrieved evidence, the most obese Canadian province is Newfoundland and Labrador. A 2017/18 study found it had the highest prevalence of obesity at 39.4% [d6]. Earlier data from 2004 also indicated Newfoundland and Labrador had the highest obesity rate among provinces at 34% [d2]. More recent data from 2023 identifies Alberta as having the highest share of overweight adults, but this is a different metric from obesity [d1].
